headline:
Learning more.
With less.
intro: I develop data-efficient visual and multimodal foundation models that learn useful, structured representations with less supervision.
bio: I am a Lecturer at the University of Surrey, jointly appointed in the Centre for Vision, Speech and Signal Processing (CVSSP) and the Surrey Institute for People-Centred Artificial Intelligence (PAI). Previously, I was a Surrey Future Fellow (2023–2026) and a Research Fellow (2021–2023).

My research focuses on self-supervised learning, visual foundation models and multimodal AI. I am particularly interested in how models discover meaningful concepts, connect information across modalities, and transfer to new tasks efficiently. I also work on applications in healthcare and scientific imaging.

research.title: Visual foundation models
research.text: Self-supervised learning, masked image modelling and concept-aware representations that reduce reliance on large labelled datasets.

research.title: Multimodal understanding
research.text: Connecting vision, audio and language through efficient adaptation, information flow and interpretable multimodal representations.

research.title: AI for health and science
research.text: Transferable visual representations for medical, microscopy and multi-channel images, with a focus on robustness across datasets.
